### 4. `CER_Type_Relationship_Matrix.md`

# C.E.R. — Type Relationship Matrix

Status: **in progress / draft — first full pass complete, several soft calls flagged for review.** This is the 18×18 elemental-relationship system underlying Affinity: not a re-skin of Pokémon's real type chart, but a *from-scratch, symmetric* relationship system that uses the real chart as a starting prompt and overrides it wherever thematic logic (energy, not combat) says something different. Referenced by `affinity-architecture.md` (the wheel) and `world-architecture.md` (regional World Affinity adjacency); this doc is the source of record for the relationships themselves.

## What Affinity actually is (the foundation this matrix sits on)

Settled 2026-09-18, in the session that produced this matrix:

- **Affinity** is energy itself — never the mechanism or process, the *reason* mechanisms can operate. It shows itself in different forms depending on what it interacts with (a passive stat, a gameplay trigger, a distribution weight) but is one substance, not several systems sharing a name.
- **World Affinity** = the world's life essence — an ambient "nature's aura" — split into 18 equally-powerful elemental sources. Regional (biome/Anchor-scale, not global, not tiny "pockets"), with adjacent regions meant to physically collide/blend at their borders — this matrix is what governs *how* they blend.
- **Trainer Affinity** = a trainer's assimilation/molding of that world energy — what they've been around, how that element's fundamentals respond to their actions and character. Both a behavior record *and* an eligibility gate: actions earn eligibility, but activating a type is a deliberate, meaningful choice on top of that (see `affinity-architecture.md`'s wheel section for the commitment-gate proposal).
- **Resonance** = a separate measure from Affinity — how strongly a trainer's connection to an energy can be shared with a specific partner Pokémon through their bond (Ash-Greninja). Affinity is "how much/what kind"; Resonance is "how well it transfers." Scope (per-partner vs. per-type ceiling) still open.
- **No negative/opposing values.** All "gone wrong" states are corruption's job, not Affinity's — Affinity itself is purely non-negative across all 18 types. Opposition is a *selection/coexistence* rule, not a stat penalty.

## The four relationship categories

Every one of the 153 unique type pairs falls into exactly one of these, **defaulting to Neutral unless a real thematic case promotes it** — this table is expected to grow/get refined over time, not be authored perfectly in one pass (see "Soft calls" below).

- **Opposed** — mutual cancellation, like two wavelengths meeting and both becoming zero ("wet and dry," "hot and cold"). The two types physically cannot coexist — cannot both be active on the Trainer Affinity wheel, and (pending confirmation) likely can't dominate the same World Affinity region without one collapsing the other.
- **Suppressive** — asymmetric. One type is weakened by the other's presence; the other is unaffected. Both types can still coexist/be co-selected — this is a one-sided penalty, not exclusion. Confirmed to apply in **both** contexts (wheel and world-adjacency), but with a **different expression per context** — e.g. Fire/Water suppresses as a stat penalty on the wheel, but as active extinguishing/hardening in the world. Every Suppressive pair below still needs its own wheel-effect and world-effect written up individually; only the category and direction are locked so far.
- **Harmonic** — mutual, positive interaction between two *different* types (e.g. Bug/Grass: ecosystem reinforcement; Steel/Electric: conduction/power, both directions). Distinct from same-type reinforcement (below) — Harmonic pairs are two different energies actively complementing each other, not one energy doubling down on itself.
- **Neutral** — the default. No interaction either direction. Can be promoted out of Neutral in the *world/nature* context if a real case exists (the same way Electric/Ground was pulled out of Neutral); in the *trainer/wheel* context, Neutral stays flat — no effect, both freely selectable, no further elaboration needed since there's no "environment" for a subtler interaction to happen in.

**Same-type pairing is not part of this 18×18 grid at all** — it's a separate, context-scoped rule. In the *world/regional* context, two adjacent same-type regions reinforce/boost each other. In the *Trainer Affinity/wheel* context, this is structurally moot: a trainer only has one slot per type, so there's nothing to pair.

## The full matrix — first pass (all 153 pairs categorized)

Listed as one row per type, only non-Neutral relationships and explicitly-flagged immunity-style Neutrals shown; every pair not listed under a type defaults to plain Neutral.

**Opposed (3 pairs, mutual, no direction):**
- Fire ↔ Water
- Fire ↔ Ice
- Dragon ↔ Fairy

**Suppressive (28 pairs, directional — "A weakens B"):**
- Fighting weakens Normal
- Fire weakens Grass
- Fire weakens Bug
- Fire weakens Ground
- Electric weakens Water
- Water weakens Rock
- Water weakens Steel *(soft call — see below)*
- Ground weakens Electric
- Electric weakens Flying
- Ice weakens Grass
- Ice weakens Ground
- Ice weakens Flying
- Ice weakens Dragon
- Steel weakens Ice
- Fighting weakens Ice
- Ground weakens Poison
- Poison weakens Fairy
- Rock weakens Flying
- Flying weakens Bug
- Flying weakens Fighting
- Bug weakens Psychic
- Dark weakens Psychic *(soft call — see below)*
- Psychic weakens Fighting
- Fighting weakens Rock
- Steel weakens Dragon
- Fairy weakens Dark
- Fighting weakens Dark
- Fighting weakens Steel
- Fighting weakens Fairy

**Harmonic (19 pairs, mutual):**
- Fire — Steel
- Fire — Rock *(soft call — see below)*
- Water — Grass
- Water — Ice *(flagged "strong" — possible first candidate for a Harmonic sub-degree if the category ever needs numeric weight)*
- Water — Ground
- Electric — Steel
- Electric — Psychic
- Grass — Bug *(the original confirmed example)*
- Grass — Poison
- Grass — Ground
- Poison — Bug
- Ground — Rock
- Ground — Steel
- Ground — Bug *(soft call — see below)*
- Flying — Dragon
- Psychic — Fairy
- Psychic — Ghost
- Dark — Ghost
- Rock — Steel

**Explicitly-flagged immunity-style Neutrals** (no interaction either direction, called out specifically because a real chart immunity backs the call): Normal/Ghost, Poison/Steel, Ground/Flying, Fighting/Ghost.

**Everything else** (~99 pairs) — plain default Neutral, no forced justification attempted.

## Soft calls — flagged for a second look, not broken, just lower-confidence

- **Water/Steel (Suppressive, Steel weakened)** — rust logic, real but slower/subtler than the other Suppressive pairs. Worth confirming it's worth having a relationship at all vs. just leaving Neutral.
- **Fire/Rock vs. Fire/Ground** — both had a legitimate volcanic-imagery claim; Rock was given sole ownership of the Harmonic "lava" niche, Ground was instead made Suppressive ("scorched earth"). An arbitration call, not a forced answer.
- **Ground/Bug (Harmonic)** — picked soil-ecology/decomposition logic over the real chart's Suppressive-leaning read (burial/exposure). Reasonable either way.
- **Psychic/Dark (Suppressive, Psychic weakened)** — the least thematically "obvious" of the Suppressive calls; accepted on "deception/intrusive shadow overwhelms rational thought" but worth a second look.

## Open questions this matrix still needs answered

- **Does Opposed also block two regions from dominating the same World Affinity boundary**, or is Opposed strictly a Trainer Affinity wheel rule? (Mirrors the general "does Suppressive apply in both contexts" question, which was already answered yes — Opposed's cross-context behavior hasn't been explicitly confirmed.)
- **Does Harmonic carry a real numeric bonus, or is it purely "the good version of Neutral" with no mechanical delta?** Water/Ice being flagged "strong" implies degrees might eventually matter — not decided yet.
- **Dual-typed Pokémon spanning an Opposed pair** (e.g. a Fire/Water-type partner, if Cobblemon has one) — what does that mean for Resonance/Trainer Affinity with that specific partner? Raised earlier, not yet resolved. Options on the table: such pairings are avoided by design in which types get marked Opposed, or a Pokémon holding both is narratively exceptional (Fractured-adjacent) rather than ordinary.
- **Each Suppressive pair still needs its individual wheel-effect and world-effect written up** — only the category, direction, and two worked examples (Fire/Water, Electric/Ground) currently have real prose behind them; the other 26 Suppressive pairs are categorized but not yet flavor-written.
- **Resonance scope** — per-partner-Pokémon, per-type ceiling, or both (a per-type ceiling that a specific partner-bond fills toward)? Raised in the same session, not yet resolved.
- **Wheel commitment mechanic** — leaning toward eligibility-threshold-to-unlock plus a deliberate commitment act at a Resonance Anchor (with cooldown/cost) to actually swap an active slot, rather than free-toggle — proposed, not yet locked as final.
- **Region shape** — radial falloff from an Anchor (energies blend gradually, contested overlap zones at borders) vs. hard biome-boundary segments — proposed radial falloff to support "regions collide and merge," not yet locked as final.
- **Death/Resonance penalty** — Wesley referenced an existing "resonance penalty" idea for player death but its actual shape hasn't been given yet; needed before persistence rules can be finalized.
### 5. `CER_Shadow_Fractured_Identity_Design.md`

# C.E.R. — Shadow & Fractured Pokémon Identity Design

Status: **open design proposal, not yet built** — recovered from a pre-compaction session transcript on 2026-09-19 and logged here in full per Wesley's "log everything" instruction. Nothing below has been implemented; treat this as the design brief to build against once prioritized. Full verbatim source preserved in `claude/CER_ChatGPT_Import_Integration.md`.

This doc covers two of C.E.R.'s "exceptional categories" referenced in `overview.md` — **Shadow** and **Fractured** — plus their surprising cross-connection.

---

## 1. Shadow Pokémon — design goal

Wesley's explicit brief: don't make Shadow just another "black recolor" reused from Pixelmon/Cobblemon servers/fan content. Shadow should have its own identity — a player should recognize a C.E.R. Shadow Pokémon by its *behavior*, not just its palette — and removing the Shadow state should feel like a real, weighed decision, not an automatic upgrade.

### 1.1 Core philosophy

**Shadow Pokémon are powerful, unstable, and useful precisely because they're dangerous.** Not "Normal → Shadow = stronger," but "Normal → Shadow = altered risk/reward Pokémon."

### 1.2 Shadow Resonance (combat resource)

Every Shadow Pokémon has an internal **Shadow Resonance** meter. It rises from: dealing damage, taking damage, landing super-effective hits, using Shadow moves, getting hit by certain attacks, or experiencing certain status conditions.

Three states, each changing behavior:
- **Stable** — normal Shadow benefits.
- **Resonant** — small offensive/defensive bonuses.
- **Frenzied** — big power spike (increased damage, crit chance, priority/speed, empowered Shadow moves) at a cost (reduced defense, increased incoming damage, chance of losing control, some moves become stronger but riskier).

### 1.3 Shadow-exclusive move family

Not "Shadow Ball but better" — a genuine move family communicating that Shadow energy is a *state/force*, not another elemental type:
- **Shadow Pulse** — Dark/Ghost-esque attack, scales with Shadow Resonance.
- **Shadow Break** — bonus damage vs. stat-boosted targets.
- **Umbral Rush** — priority attack that raises instability.
- **Void Claw** — high crit, causes recoil.
- **Shadow Drain** — damage + heal, raises instability.
- **Eclipse** — powerful field-affecting move, temporarily alters battlefield conditions.

### 1.4 Shadow is a state, not a 19th type

Explicit design rule: **don't create a "Shadow type."** A Shadow Lucario stays Fighting/Steel and carries a separate **Shadow State** layered on top. Keeps typing math (and the Type Relationship Matrix) untouched, and prevents Shadow from becoming "just another type slot."

### 1.5 Shadow ability pool

Not one universal Shadow ability — a pool, so two Shadow Pokémon don't play identically:
- **Umbral Adaptation** — temporary offensive boost after taking a super-effective hit.
- **Shadow Surge** — Shadow moves strengthen below 50% HP.
- **Predatory Instinct** — bonus damage vs. weakened targets.
- **Dark Resonance** — certain attacks raise Shadow Resonance.
- **Unstable Core** — big power, occasional recoil.
- **Abyssal Skin** — reduced damage from certain attacks, but status effects last longer.

### 1.6 Interaction with Affinity — "Corrupted Affinity"

Shadow Pokémon may not carry normal Affinity — instead a **Corrupted Affinity** that fluctuates by environment (e.g. a Shadow Jolteon in a highly-charged area could react with Electric Affinity and gain a temporary "Overcharged Shadow" effect/move; a Shadow Vaporeon would react differently in a Water-affinity region). Ties Shadow directly into the world-affinity/region system rather than existing independently of it.

### 1.7 Environmental behavior & Shadow Outbreaks

Normal Pokémon spawn because a biome supports them; **Shadow Pokémon appear where something is wrong** — around corrupted structures, certain ruins, specific weather, or during a **Shadow Outbreak**: a temporary world event where Shadow spawn rate/rarity/strength spikes, special research objectives unlock, players can investigate the source, and a boss/alpha Shadow may appear at the end. Ties Shadow into exploration, research, quests, worldgen, and progression simultaneously rather than being a flat spawn-table entry.

### 1.8 Capture behavior

Not identical to normal capture — a **suppression mechanic**: the player weakens a Shadow Pokémon's Resonance before capture, aided by purification items, Affinity items, research equipment, or specialized Poké Balls. Gives players an actual reason to prepare for Shadow encounters.

### 1.9 Branching resolution — Purify / Stabilize / Remain Shadow

This is flagged as potentially C.E.R.'s single most distinctive Shadow mechanic. Purification is **not** a one-way "delete the Shadow" button:
- **Keep Shadow** — retain Shadow abilities/moves/Resonance/appearance/research classification as-is.
- **Purify** — gain purified traits/different ability pool/different moves/possible stat changes/unique research completion.
- **Stabilize** (a third path) — don't remove the Shadow energy, learn to *control* it: **Unstable Shadow → Stabilized Shadow → Mastered Shadow**, each stage less volatile and unlocking more advanced Shadow abilities, ending in a unique cosmetic effect/move/ability at Mastered. The final form isn't "purified" — it's "a Shadow Pokémon the player learned to control."

### 1.10 Shadow research tree (Field Guide integration)

Observe → Study (observe Shadow Resonance) → Battle (defeat one) → Capture → Control (stabilize) → Purify → Master (successfully use Shadow abilities) → Shadow Species Mastery. Makes Shadow part of the research gameplay loop, not just combat. Species-level Field Guide entries could document: first observation, first capture, Resonance behavior, preferred environments, Shadow ability, Shadow moves, purification method, stabilization method, environmental effects, lore discoveries.

### 1.11 Visual language (beyond "black Pokémon + red eyes")

Explicit anti-goal: avoid the classic black-recolor-with-red-eyes trap. Proposed grammar: dark particulate/energy effects, floating particles, distorted aura, smoke-like energy, flickering outlines; eyes with glowing/irregular/species-specific distortion rather than universal red; distorted silhouettes, energy leaking from specific body areas, cracks/veins of Shadow energy, floating fragments, flickering textures; animation quirks (idle spasms, unusual breathing, energy pulses, distorted attack animations, different battle-entrance effects) so the player recognizes a Shadow by behavior before recognizing the species.

**Species-specific manifestation examples given:** Shadow Charizard (dark/unstable flames), Shadow Gyarados (electrical-storm-like aura), Shadow Lucario (Aura-concentrated energy), Shadow Gengar (partially intangible body, leaking energy) — the same underlying system should manifest differently per species so it never reads as a universal recolor.

### 1.12 Shadow evolution (optional, selective)

Some species could have **Shadow-specific evolution conditions** producing a distinct form not reachable normally (e.g. Shadow Eevee → an undecided unique branch). Explicitly not proposed for every species — selective, to keep it special.

### 1.13 Team-composition mechanics

Multiple Shadows on one team could raise collective Resonance (1 Shadow = minor bonus, 2 = stronger, 3+ = dangerous instability) — a strategic "do I build a Shadow-heavy team?" question, with cost attached so it doesn't collapse into "always run six Shadows."

### 1.14 Non-combat utility (world-interaction tool, not just battle variant)

Proposed Shadow-exclusive interactions: **Shadow Sight** (detect hidden structures), **Shadow Sense** (detect nearby rare Pokémon), **Shadow Resonance** (reveal corrupted areas), **Umbral Interaction** (activate ancient machinery), **Shadow Tracking** (follow traces of certain Pokémon) — makes a Shadow Pokémon a genuine exploration tool, not merely a combat pick.

### 1.15 Camera/research-system tie-in

Photographing a Shadow Pokémon under specific conditions could reveal Shadow-specific research entries (e.g. "Shadow Resonance Pattern," "Rare Shadow Behavior") documentable only through photography — lets a player become a "Shadow researcher" without building a Shadow battle team. Research levels could progressively reveal usable world-knowledge (e.g. "Shadow Pokémon exhibit increased resonance in regions containing high concentrations of [Affinity]" → later, species-specific resonance behavior), turning research into a tool for actually locating rare Shadows.

### 1.16 Rare Shadow anomalies

Occasional variant Shadow encounters beyond the baseline: **Resonant Shadow** (unusually powerful), **Ancient Shadow** (found near ancient structures), **Feral Shadow** (extremely aggressive), **Stable Shadow** (naturally low instability), **Apex Shadow** (very rare, exceptionally strong), **Affinity-Touched Shadow** (Shadow energy has interacted with a specific Affinity).

### 1.17 Scope discipline — the proposed "pick 4-6 pillars" list

Explicit caution against building all of the above — Shadow shouldn't become "an entire second Pokémon game." The proposed polished-pillar set (**awaiting Wesley's confirmation, not yet locked**):

1. Distinct visual identity (species-specific manifestation, never a flat recolor).
2. Shadow State (layered on existing typing, not a 19th type).
3. Shadow Resonance (the combat risk/reward resource).
4. Shadow-exclusive moves/abilities.
5. Purify vs. Stabilize vs. Remain Shadow (the long-term player decision).
6. Shadow Research (Field Guide + photography + exploration + quests, all touching Shadow).

**Signature framing line:** *"Shadow Pokémon are not inherently evil or simply stronger. They're unstable. The player gradually learns how to live with them."*

---

## 2. Fractured Pokémon — the Poké Synchro Device pivot

This idea was triggered directly by the Shadow-identity discussion above, giving C.E.R.'s three "special variant" categories a clean, non-overlapping identity split:

- **Shadow** = corrupted / dangerous / power-focused.
- **Fractured** = incomplete / unstable / resonance-focused.
- **Fusion** = complete synthesis / deliberate combination.

### 2.1 Core rule (locked framing, pending build)

**Only Fractured Pokémon can be Synchro'd, because only Fractured Pokémon require a second consciousness to achieve temporary stability.** A Fractured Pokémon is missing pieces of its body/energy/dimensional structure and is normally too unstable to interface with. The Poké Synchro Device doesn't "control" it — the trainer becomes the missing stabilizing component. **The trainer doesn't fuse with the Fractured Pokémon; the trainer completes the resonance that lets the Fractured Pokémon exist in a stable state.**

This is explicitly meant to be locked in as a foundational rule before any other Fractured-variant design work happens, because it reframes every subsequent design question as: *"What does this Pokémon become capable of when a human consciousness temporarily completes its fracture?"*

### 2.2 Synchro grants world-interaction abilities, not just combat buffs

While synced, a Fractured Pokémon's abilities manifest as abilities the *player* can use in the world — not merely bigger battle numbers. Example sketch (Fractured Lucario): fracture energy visible around the player, dramatically stronger Aura abilities, ability to interact with intangible fracture objects, perceive fracture anomalies, temporarily stabilize nearby fractured entities, perform a "Resonance Burst," and interact with dimensional tears normal players can't.

### 2.3 Instability risk while synced

The longer a player stays synced, the more unstable the resonance: **Stabilized → Strained → Critical**, with visual distortion, screen effects, growing power (and growing risk) as instability rises — abilities strengthen, but attacks can become unpredictable, the Pokémon may forcibly eject the player, and the environment can be left with temporary fractures. Deliberate "should I push it further?" tension, matching the pillar of Fractured = risk/utility rather than raw power.

### 2.4 Niche separation from Shadow/Fusion

- Normal Pokémon = reliable.
- Shadow Pokémon = powerful/dangerous.
- **Fractured Pokémon = utility/exploration/resonance** (not necessarily the strongest Pokémon).
- Fusion Pokémon = unique combined form/specialized power.

Keeps the categories from competing for the same "best Pokémon" slot.

### 2.5 Type-based Resonance abilities (the adopted structure over pure species-locking)

Initial idea was fully species-specific abilities (e.g. only Fractured Gengar can phase). Refined, at Wesley's suggestion, into a **two-layer type+species system** to avoid a "go find the one specific species" mandatory-Pokémon problem:

**Layer 1 — Type = the fundamental Resonance capability.** Any suitably Fractured Pokémon of a given type gets that type's baseline interaction:
- **Ghost Resonance** — phase through designated fracture barriers, enter fracture shadows, interact with intangible fracture objects, perceive spectral/fracture traces.
- **Psychic Resonance** — move resonance objects remotely, read psychic echoes, reveal hidden dimensional structures.
- **Electric Resonance** — interface with fractured machinery, redirect electrical anomalies, power dormant systems.
- **Fighting Resonance** — break/stabilize physical fracture structures, resist unstable environments, force-based resonance interactions.
- **Water Resonance** — interact with resonance currents, stabilize corrupted waterways, traverse unstable aquatic environments.

(These five are the ones sketched in the transcript; the remaining 13 types are unassigned — an open follow-up item, see Unanswered Questions.)

**Layer 2 — Species = a smaller unique trait layered on top of the type baseline**, so same-type Pokémon share a language but never feel redundant. Examples given: Fractured Gengar's **Shadowstep** (longer fracture-shadow dwell, movement between connected fracture pockets) vs. Fractured Mismagius's **Hex Echo** (reads magical/fracture echoes other Ghosts can't) vs. Fractured Rotom's **Possession** (temporarily inhabits fractured machinery) — all three are Ghost Resonance, but distinct.

**Dual-typing combines both Resonances** (e.g. Fractured Lucario = Fighting's physical-stabilization Force Resonance + Steel's Metal Resonance for conducting/redirecting resonance through metal objects, plus a species trait like Aura Sense).

**Tiered depth within a type** is also proposed (e.g. Ghost Resonance: Phase I = pass through thin barriers → Phase II = enter fracture shadows → Phase III, rare/species-specific = travel between connected fracture spaces) so not every Pokémon of a type performs identically.

**Ability categories** (to keep the system from collapsing into pure traversal/"Zelda dungeon key" design): Traversal (phase, swim through unstable matter, climb fracture surfaces, short teleport), Environmental manipulation (stabilize/destroy/redirect/energize/freeze/purify), Investigation (detect resonance, read echoes, reveal hidden structures, track anomalies), Combat (fracture-specific attacks/resonance interactions/environmental combat effects), World interaction (repair machines, possess technology, communicate with echoes, manipulate objects).

**Design rule locked as the generative principle:** *Type determines what a Fractured Pokémon can do. Species determines how it does it.* Extended further: *Types provide the language. Species provide the accent. Research teaches the player how to speak it. Synchro lets the player speak it themselves.*

### 2.6 Research-system tie-in

Mirrors the Shadow research-tree approach: a newly-found Fractured Pokémon starts as "Resonance Behavior: Unknown," then reveals observed behavior, then a hypothesis (e.g. "Ghost-type resonance permits temporary interaction with nonphysical structures"), then a confirmed property, then species-variation discoveries (e.g. "Gengar can maintain phase-state significantly longer than other Ghost-type Fractures"). Also proposes that individual Fractured Pokémon of the *same* species can have slightly different resonance behavior (not randomized to the point of noise, but enough to reward research), with a possible lore explanation: "Fracture behavior is influenced by both biological species and the nature of the fracture that produced it."

### 2.7 Sync moves as real spell effects (Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks integration)

Wesley's idea: when synced, pressing a Pokémon's move key should **directly trigger the real spell effect** an equivalent Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks scroll/book would cast — the move keypress *becomes* the right-click/cast event, bypassing the scroll/book UI entirely. Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks exposes a real API for registering custom spells and schools, so this is buildable as genuine custom spell behavior rather than a cosmetic reskin:

`Pokémon Move pressed → check move's assigned spell/effect → invoke spell → consume PP/cooldown → resolve effect`

Example mapping sketch for a synced Fractured Charizard: Flamethrower → actual Cobblemon move behavior; Fireball → Iron's Fireball behavior; Air Slash → custom projectile; Heat Wave → custom AoE spell; Dragon Pulse → custom magic projectile. Not limited to Iron's existing spell list — new custom Ars/Iron's-style spells can be authored specifically for the Pokémon-move system.

### 2.8 Existing mod precedent for the UX pattern

**Cobblemon: Synchro Machine** already lets a player morph into and play as a Pokémon, with Z/X/C/V mapped to moves 1–4, and experimental support for starting a normal Cobblemon turn-based battle while morphed — confirms the basic "Pokémon moves become player keybinds" UX is buildable/precedented. Also noted in the same research pass: Cobblemon Quick Battle and SV-style auto-battle mods (direct attack resolution without the traditional battle screen), and that Cobblemon's normal turn-based battle already runs on Pokémon Showdown under the hood.

### 2.9 Three-layer combat architecture (proposed, not built)

1. **Normal Pokémon moves** — untouched, standard Cobblemon/Showdown battle screen.
2. **Fractured Pokémon Sync moves** — real-world Minecraft abilities on Z/X/C/V while synced; each move individually backed by either a Cobblemon move effect, an Iron's Spells effect, or a fully custom C.E.R. ability.
3. **Titan fights** — proposed as the payoff use case: a Fractured Pokémon synced against a physically-moving, dodging, terrain-destroying Titan boss, aiming at it with Z/X/C/V abilities in real time rather than a static battle-screen HP bar. Recommendation: keep authentic Cobblemon/Showdown move data and type logic underneath the action layer, and let only the visual/physical manifestation be Minecraft-side action combat — "Pokémon-authentic damage/type logic without sacrificing the giant cinematic Minecraft boss fight."

**Framing line for why Sync moves manifest physically at all:** *A normal Pokémon performs a move according to its natural battle mechanics. A Fractured Pokémon has an unstable connection between Pokémon energy and the physical world, allowing certain moves to manifest directly into Minecraft's physical/magical systems.*

### 2.10 Recommended build approach

Treat this as C.E.R.'s own integration layer (a "Move → Effect Adapter" system) rather than trying to force one existing mod to own the whole feature — reusing Iron's Spells' custom-spell API, Cobblemon's move/Showdown data, and Cobblemon: Synchro Machine's keybind-UX precedent as the three source ingredients.

---

## 3. Open items carried from this design pass

- Which ~13 remaining Pokémon types get a defined Fracture Resonance ability (only Ghost/Psychic/Electric/Fighting/Water are sketched above).
- Confirm the Shadow "6 pillars" scope list (§1.17) as the actual build target, or trim/expand it.
- Decide whether Shadow's "Corrupted Affinity" mechanic (§1.6) is compatible with however Affinity's spatial model (grid-diffusion vs. Anchor/radial-falloff, still unresolved — see item #19 in `CER_Unanswered_Questions.md`) ends up working.
- Build-order question: does Fractured/Synchro depend on Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks being in the final mod list, or does it need a from-scratch custom-spell layer regardless?
- No MMI entries yet exist for **Cobblemon: Synchro Machine**, **Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks**, or a dedicated "Poké Synchro Device" mod — none of these were previously tiered in `CER_Master_Mod_Index.md`. Flagged as a follow-up mod-research task, not yet done.
### 6. `research-system.md`

# C.E.R. — Research System & Field Guide

Status: in progress / draft. Covers the Research System Charter (who owns what), the Field Guide UI/UX design, the Cobblemon Snap discovery that reframed the whole system, the two-camera resolution, and the open variant-tracking question.

## Research System Charter (proposed, awaiting sign-off)

Divides research duties across four systems so they don't compete for the same job:

- **Cobblemon Snap** owns photographic/observational research: encounter, photograph, pose, activity, habitat documentation, Snapdex progression.
- **Cobblemon Research Tasks** owns active/interactive research: catching, battling, breeding, evolving, item use, move use — things done *to or with* the Pokémon rather than observed.
- **Field Journal** (custom, built on top of both) owns the narrative layer: player notes, favorite photos, discovered lore, world/biome context.
- **FTB Quests** owns the campaign/expedition layer: "go to this place," multi-step story content that isn't about a single species.

No system tries to do another's job; the Field Guide UI (below) is the single front-end window into all four, not an implementation itself.

## Major discovery — Cobblemon Snap as the research backbone

Snap turned out to be substantially more complete than any research-system idea built from scratch, prompting a full re-architecture:

- Photographs scored on distance/framing/behavior-activity/facing/conditions; multi-Pokémon group photos supported.
- **5 built-in research levels per species**; tracks forms, poses/activities, biomes, shiny records, best score, total photos.
- 3D Pokémon presentation + species entry + gallery.
- **Tasks are fully datapack-customizable**: id/title/description/trigger/target/amount, item + CobbleDollar + command rewards; default tasks exportable/editable and live-reloadable via `/snap reload`. Confirmed strong.
- **Task/research "tabs" or categories are NOT confirmed customizable** — Snapdex's page structure (Pokémon entries/Dex view/Gallery view/Tasks page) isn't documented as arbitrarily re-categorizable. Open unknown, not assumed impossible. Workaround: treat each Pokémon's own entry as the de facto "research file," organizing tasks conceptually (Habitat Study/Behavioral Study/Social Study/Environmental Study/Rare Observation) rather than needing literal UI tabs.
- **Cobblemon: Research Tasks** (companion mod — 5–8 hand-authored tasks per species for all 1,025 species, in-game task editor with add/delete/live-edit/save-load presets) runs alongside Snap rather than replacing it — this is the Charter's "active/interactive" half.
- **Open research task (not yet done):** map Snap's full set of trigger types against C.E.R.'s wishlist (biome-specific photo, time-of-day, weather, cross-species pairs, specific-move-in-use, alpha/rare-variant, near-structure) to confirm real trigger-system coverage before fully committing to Snap as the backbone.

This means the research system may not need to be built from scratch — mostly configured/extended rather than invented.

## Variant/Phenomena tracking (Shiny/Shadow/Fractured/Fusion) — open technical question

Snap already tracks forms/poses/activities/biomes/shiny/best-score/total-photos per species, which suggests a Variant/Phenomena research structure is plausible: Shiny / Shadow / Fractured / Fusion / Forms as explicit, **non-mutually-exclusive** categories (a Shadow-Shiny should satisfy both Shiny and Shadow research simultaneously).

**Unresolved:** whether Snap's research system can recognize **arbitrary Cobblemon aspects/forms** (Shadow/Fractured/Fusion would "just work" if implemented as Cobblemon aspects) versus Snap hardcoding shiny-detection specifically (would require a companion mod/datapack/KubeJS layer to extend it). Best-guess opinion leans toward "hardcoded to shiny only," since Shadow/Fractured/Fusion are custom aspects introduced after Snap's author wrote it — but this is an opinion, not a confirmed answer. Needs a real verification pass (inspect Snap's source or ask its author). Tracked in `claude/CER_Unanswered_Questions.md`.

If Snap can't natively extend, the plan is to build variant tracking in the Field Journal layer instead (custom KubeJS/data layer reading Cobblemon's aspect data directly), with Snap continuing to own vanilla shiny/species/behavior tracking. Fusion specifically is also flagged as possibly belonging in its own Species Index entry rather than a Variants-page tab, since a Fusion result is arguably a distinct creature rather than a variant of one parent (see Field Guide mockup below).

## Cameras — resolved into two tools (was three overlapping ideas)

A generic "handheld camera" placeholder, Exposure (film/developing/physical photography), and Snap's own camera all covered overlapping ground across separate discussions. Resolved:

- **Cobblemon Snap's camera** — the field-research instrument, owns the Field Guide's photographic evidence per the Charter above.
- **Exposure** — the personal/artistic instrument: scenery, printable physical photographs, camera stands, developing — no research scoring, for players who want photography as its own hobby. Confirmed current 1.21.1 Fabric/Forge/NeoForge/Quilt support (v1.9.18).
- The generic "handheld camera" placeholder is **retired** — Snap's camera already covers what it was standing in for.
- **Open verification:** whether Exposure's photograph/entity data (reportedly carries subject info in its photo NBT) is actually readable by KubeJS/FTB Quests/Cobblemon triggers. Matters less for research mechanics now that Snap owns that job, but still matters if Exposure photos should trigger anything beyond being decorative/personal. Tracked in Unanswered Questions.

## Field Guide UI/UX

**Locked visual language** (confirmed against a generated mockup): red-bound digital field notebook, embossed page-cards as navigation, silhouettes for undiscovered Pokémon, sprites/photographs for discovered ones, nested Document → Section → Entry → Detail navigation, physical-tab section navigation. Design law: *it shouldn't feel like a menu pretending to be a book — it should feel like a notebook that happens to function as a menu.* This is specific enough to stop scope creep (e.g. a future "holographic sci-fi Pokédex" reskin proposal).

**Mechanical baseline updated:** the original mod comparison (Field Guide mod / Patchouli / Modonomicon / Field Notes / Scholar / Guide / Cobblemon Field Guide) predates the Snap discovery above. Snap + Research Tasks now cover most of what a standalone "Field Guide" mod's discovery backend would give, mechanically, and better (Cobblemon-native). Field Guide/Patchouli's job is narrowed to what Snap/Research Tasks **don't** cover: non-Pokémon discoveries — biomes, structures, lore entries, world/Affinity concepts, Lost Biome sites.

**Confirmed structural details from the mockup** (six panels: Main Menu, Species Index, Undiscovered Entry, Discovered Entry, Variants Page, Notes/Observations):

- Main menu tabs: **Species / Biomes / Resources / Research** — confirms the division above (Species = Snap/Research Tasks' domain; Biomes/Resources = the non-Pokémon gap; Research = cross-cutting progress view).
- Variants page shows **Normal / Shiny / Shadow / Fractured** tabs (Fusion conspicuously absent — open decision, see above).
- Discovered species page's Research Progress checklist (Encountered / Photographed / Observed using an Electric-type move / Rare behavior documented) is a near-exact match for how Research Tasks structures its per-species tasks — confirms that checklist is Research Tasks' data, not hand-authored per Pokémon.
- Notes/Observations page's photo strip is explicitly captioned as coming "from Snap or the camera" — i.e. the design already assumed a Snap-research photo and a separate handheld/Exposure photo land side by side in the same journal page. Matches the two-camera resolution above exactly.
- Empty photo slots use a small camera-icon placeholder ("you haven't taken this shot yet") — worth keeping literally across every page, reinforcing discovery-through-observation.

**Proposed four-layer structure** (World Remembers: Dear Diary adopted as the primary *design reference*, not installed verbatim — its "memories worth remembering, not a spam log" philosophy):

1. **Pokédex** — objective species data.
2. **Research** — player-discovered facts (encounters, behaviors, habitats, evolution witnessed, weather/time correlations).
3. **Journal** — personal narrative (manual notes, photos, memorable encounters, milestones).
4. **World Memory** — automatically-generated significant-event log (first encounter/capture/evolution/shiny/legendary/Titan-transformation entries), tying directly into the photography and Titan systems.

**Caveat:** Dear Diary itself has no Cobblemon awareness — "automatic memory when you catch a Pikachu" isn't something it does out of the box. Plan for the Field Journal to be a parallel custom system borrowing Dear Diary's *design philosophy*, bridged via custom KubeJS hooks into Cobblemon's capture/evolution/encounter events, unless Dear Diary is confirmed to expose a public event API.

## Research → Application infrastructure

**Modest Magic** (Altar + Pedestal replacement for vanilla enchanting; Infusing/Enchanting/Summoning recipe types, datapack-customizable) proposed as the physical Research/Synthesis Altar: gives a visually-legible ritual-crafting station for Affinity Infusion without inventing a multiblock from scratch, with "Summoning" reinterpreted as Pokémon/material synthesis/manifestation rather than literal monster summoning — feeds into the Fusion Crafting (theory) → Synthesis Chamber (practice) pipeline. Recipes are datapack-driven, plugging directly into the `cer:` datapack.

## Two open verification items carried from earlier passes

- Whether the Cobblemon KubeJS Bridge exposes a "species newly scanned" event (fallback: have the Field Guide read Cobblemon's own Pokédex state directly).
- Whether Snap's command reward fires reliably per-player when tested on a real task.

### 8. `CER_Supplementary_Mod_Research.md`

# C.E.R. — Supplementary Mod Research

Reference/supporting material that doesn't belong in the main design docs: third-party mod deep-dives, the Vanilla Backport feature breakdown, the FTB Quests addon audit, and the phased build-order plan. Tiered adoption decisions live in `claude/CER_Master_Mod_Index.md`; design decisions that came out of this research live in `governance-and-workflow.md`, `research-system.md`, and `world-architecture.md`.

---

## Vanilla Backport (1.21.1 NeoForge, current 1.1.7.10)

Three-way feature classification:

**(a) Genuinely new to 1.21.1** — Pale Garden/Garden Awakens set (Eyeblossoms, Resin, Creaking/Creaking Heart); Wild Update backport (Deep Dark/Warden/Ancient Cities/Mangrove/Allay/Frog); Spring-to-Life ambience + animal variants (Temperate/Cold/Warm biome-tag-driven — see `affinity-architecture.md`'s decoupling decision); wolf variants + sound personalities; Armadillos; Happy Ghast/Dried Ghast/Chase-the-Skies set; worldgen/attribute technical infrastructure (bounciness/air_drag_modifier/friction_modifier, new IntProviders, surface rules).

**(b) Already exists in base 1.21.1, gets the newer implementation** — Bundles (modern UI/controls/dye/legacy-toggle), leash physics, camel spawning logic, creative-tab presentation.

**(c) Bundled non-backport original content — flag for separate review** — Sulfur Caves biome, Cinnabar/Sulfur block sets, Sulfur Cube archetype system. Not a real vanilla-future feature; shouldn't be accepted as part of "vanilla parity." **Proposal:** split into two M.M.I. entries — `Vanilla Backport — Vanilla Content` and `Vanilla Backport — Chaos Cubed (bonus content)` — so a future audit can drop the Sulfur/Cinnabar half without re-litigating whether the rest stays.

Namespace migrates `vanillabackport:` → `minecraft:` for forward/resource-pack compatibility; per-feature config toggles mean the mod is safe to adopt selectively.

**Pot storage (decorated-pot-as-small-storage):** interact with a placed pot to store items; contents persist with the block; pot stays visually a pot, not a chest; explicitly small-capacity, not a chest replacement. VB patched a bug where pots lost contents on reload/dimension-change. Proposed use: distributed small-capacity flavor storage in labs/ranches/field stations (Apricorns/Poké Balls/evolution items/fossils in a research lab; samples/Resin/Affinity materials in a research station; seeds/berries/feed on a ranch) instead of walls of chests. **Open verification:** exact per-pot item capacity and interaction behavior in C.E.R.'s specific 1.21.1/NeoForge setup.

## Trainer ecosystem (Poké Belt / Cobblemon Trainers)

- **Pokébelt** — dedicated trainer-belt Poké Ball storage/equipment concept, Fabric-only at time of research, no confirmed NeoForge port. **Proposal:** drop it in favor of reskinning a Vanilla Backport Bundle as a "Trainer's Belt" (custom texture + name in the resource pack) — gets the fantasy for free with zero new dependencies. *(Superseded 2026-09-19 — Wesley confirmed Poké Belt is kept in the MMI as-is; see `CER_Master_Mod_Index.md`.)*
- **CobblemonTrainers (old, discontinued, 1.20.1)** — skip.
- **RCT (Radical Cobblemon Trainers) API + Run & Bun** — modern stack: 1,500+ trainers, series/progression, level caps, Trainer Card, natural spawning (RCT); advanced trainer AI — move selection, switching, damage prediction, weather/terrain/abilities/hazards (Run & Bun). Strong candidate as the trainer-based progression layer: world exploration → trainer battle → rewards → research/progression unlock → level cap increase → stronger areas/trainers → bosses/Titans.
- **Cobblemon Trainers (newer project)** — singles/doubles/triples, Battle Phone, trainer categories/locks, Showdown import, Mega/Z-Move/Dynamax/Tera support — noted as a further disambiguation point from the above; not yet decided how it relates to RCT/Run & Bun.

## Storage & laboratory GUI concepts

- **Remote Access** (workstation-switcher: open one nearby workstation, cycle to others without closing the GUI, ~5-block radius) — evaluated as **design-principle inspiration, not a dependency**, for a "Tinkers-style dynamic laboratory GUI": a Research Table/Affinity Laboratory interface that dynamically exposes tabs (Research/Analysis/Processing/Infusion/Synthesis) based on which physical machine blocks are actually built nearby. Genuinely custom development, not a "find the right mod" problem — downgraded to a stretch goal (see governance proposals); design the lab blocks to work fine as separate machines first. Related precedent: Remote UI Terminal, Proxy.
- **Vanilla Storage Interface** (searchable/sortable terminal attached to an existing chest/barrel/Shulker, auto-packing, portable via Ender Chest/held Shulker) — the player-facing access layer for a "Stager"-style idea: Physical storage → Vanilla Storage Interface → Stager/processing infrastructure → machines/research/crafting. Explicitly preferred over a Refined-Storage-style fully digital network. **Open verification:** NeoForge build status (was Fabric-only at time of research) — same Bridge-Eligible Mod Principle treatment as Pokébelt.

## Small QoL / flavor mods

- **Grassier Grass** (visual tall-grass) + **Cobblemon Wild Spawn** (grass/water encounter mod using Cobblemon's own spawn data, auto-battle-start, repels/lures/type lures/shiny config) — recommended visual+mechanical pairing over the older WildEncounters datapack.
- **Lucid Advancements** (client-side advancement browser: global view, category sidebar, search, mod filtering, sorting) — recommended given how advancement-heavy C.E.R. is expected to become. Advancements = "discoveries/milestones," distinct from FTB Quests' "explicit objectives."
- **Cinematic Respawn** (client-side death→camera→fade→respawn sequence) — recommended add.
- **Crystalline** (amethyst/crystal weapon+block expansion: Divider longsword w/ Amethyst Rain & Shatter Sweep, Crusher, Gravitate; separate "Upgrade Crystalline" expansion exists) — flagged as a potential Affinity/research-crystal-technology tie-in.
- **Golden's Better Enchanting** (collectible-enchantment system via Chiseled Bookshelf book collection, unlocks enchantment levels through discovery rather than random table rolls) — strong research-progression fit.
- **The Block Box** (large vanilla-styled building/decor expansion, no worldgen) — optional building flavor.
- **OmniChest** (client-side cross-chest item search + in-world pin/beacon to the chest) — flagged as extremely useful storage QoL for a large Cobblemon world.
- **Glow Goo** (throwable light-source goo, adjustable light level) — reframed with an Affinity-recipe: Slime Ball + Electric Affinity Infusion → Glow Goo, kept as a small QoL item discovered through research rather than a full Pokémon-type-reskin item family. Other Affinity-goo variants noted as possible but not to be implemented without a real gameplay reason.
- **Useful Sleep** (config-only vanilla-sleep QoL: sleep voting, sleep-through-daytime-rain, phantom-timer reset) — add as pure QoL, explicitly not to become a progression system.
- **Build You Campfire** — flagged for later investigation once its exact functionality/compat with Unlit Campfire is confirmed.

## Cobblemon 1.8.0 → 1.8.1 → 1.7.3 version history (superseded research, kept for context)

1.8.1 was researched as a hotfix on top of 1.8.0 (Type Gem worldgen-stall fix, TM/Poké Ball fixes, NeoForge dependency crash fix, etc.), and was assessed at the time as safe/beneficial to update to. **This research predates and is superseded by the later 1.8.0→1.7.3 revert** recorded in `claude/overview.md`'s Compatibility section — the pack rolled back below both 1.8.0 and 1.8.1 once the Cobblemon-1.8-line compatibility break (Snap crash) was confirmed. Kept here as historical/superseded reasoning, not current instruction.

## FTB Quests ecosystem-addon audit (17 mods)

- **ADD:** More Quest Types (Find Entity/pose-style "field research" tasks vs. kill-quests), FTB Quests Entity Visualization (rendered 3D Pokémon in quest nodes), FTB Quests Optimizer (pure perf, no rule changes), Chest Preview.
- **ADD/TEST:** ExtraQuests (daily/weekly/key-value progression), Certain Questing Additions (UI polish/animations/EMI integration), FTB Quests Background (per-chapter themed backgrounds), Per Player Quests (solves "personal discovery shouldn't auto-complete for the whole team").
- **STRONGLY CONSIDER:** ProgressiveStages (real progression-gating framework across items/blocks/recipes/dimensions/entities, with FTB Quests+KubeJS+EMI/JEI integration — proposed as the enforcement layer under FTB Quests' presentation layer; recommended as an isolated test branch first) and Modest Magic (see `research-system.md`).
- **CONDITIONAL:** AStages FTB Quests (only if AStages wins the progression-framework decision instead of ProgressiveStages — don't run both).
- **OPTIONAL:** Achievement & Quest Tab, Open Quests API (dependency-only, don't install speculatively).
- **SKIP:** UniversalQuestTracker (solves a cross-modpack problem C.E.R. doesn't have), Open Quests Community Pack (imports someone else's questline philosophy for non-central mods), NoreQuests (revisit only if hybrid solo/ally questing becomes a real need).
- **ADD-IF-custom-music-used:** Music Trigger (flagged experimental/very young).

Overall proposed architecture: FTB Quests (presentation) → More Quest Types/Entity Viz/Background (UI+task richness) → ProgressiveStages (progression enforcement) → KubeJS/mods (actual systems) → practical application. Framed as: "the player doesn't merely complete quests, they conduct research, and research permanently changes what they can do."

## Field Guide mechanical baselines (superseded by the Snap discovery — kept for context)

Original comparison set, before Cobblemon Snap/Research Tasks were found: Field Guide mod (closest mechanical baseline — Cobblemon category, variants, journal tab, Scholar integration), Patchouli (book architecture), Modonomicon (node/index navigation), Field Notes (journal/spread presentation), Scholar (physical book UI), Guide mod (themable), Cobblemon Field Guide (dynamic lookup encyclopedia). See `claude/research-system.md` for the current, Snap-aware division of labor.

## Phased build-order plan

Phase 0 **Freeze Baseline** (launch/verify/backup as "E.R. Core Baseline — Clean") → Phase 1 **dev-structure** + Integration Candidates list (don't install yet) → Phase 2 **test Core as an actual game** (starter/party/PC/battles/evolution, open every info UI) → Phase 3 **define progression skeleton** (Survive→Explore→Catch→Research→Craft→Discover→Challenge→Master, with per-track breakdowns for Exploration/Pokémon/Research/Technology/Boss progression) → Phase 4 **first trivial KubeJS item** to prove the item→recipe→EMI/JEI pipeline → Phase 5 **lock the `er:`/`cer:` namespace convention** → Phase 6 **add exactly one real gameplay mod at a time** (backup→install→launch→test→integrate→backup cycle), starting with Grassier Grass+encounters → Phase 7 **worldgen** (Overworld baseline, then Aero Islands, then Lost/Corrupted Biomes, each tested independently) → Phase 8 **Field Guide v0.1 skeleton**, formally dividing labor between CobbleDex (species DB) / Field Guide (world knowledge) / FTB Quests (objectives) / EMI-JEI (recipes) / Patchouli (structured docs) → Phase 9 **one tiny research loop** before expanding → Phase 10 **add the "big" mods** (Trainers/Belt/grass encounters/Titans, Aero/Snap/Lost Biomes, Modest Magic/Crystalline/Glow Goo, storage stack, enchanting/combat).

**Core rule locked:** never add multiple major mods then test once — always backup→add→launch→test→integrate→backup→next.

## Post-baseline smoke test (historical — see overview.md Compatibility for current resolution)

Minecraft/Cobblemon-loads/spawning/EMI-JEI/FTB-Quests/Patchouli/KubeJS all confirmed working on a fresh instance. Two symptoms — CobbleDex not scanning/storing, and Cobblemon core player-state broken (no party interface, can't send out/recall starter, `/openstarterscreen` not reopenable) — were diagnosed as **one likely root cause** (Cobblemon client/server init or version-compat issue), not several unrelated conflicts. This is the issue later resolved by the Cobblemon 1.8.0→1.7.3 revert (see `overview.md`).

## Type-Affinity mod-fit candidates (2026-09-18)

Prompted by comparing the reworked World/Area Affinity diffusion mechanic (see `affinity-architecture.md`) against **Nature's Aura** (ambient per-chunk field that flows/diffuses, generation/drain tied to ecological triggers), **Astral Sorcery** (directional "flowing force" with an alignment quality), and **Blood Magic** (a per-chunk corruption/alignment stat that visibly mutates spawns/biome feel) as design models. Wesley asked which real mods could plug into each of the 18 type-affinities as actual gameplay content, restricted to mods with a real NeoForge 1.21.1 build (no dead/pre-1.13-era mods).

All entries below were checked against the pack's confirmed environment (Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge) via web search on 2026-09-18. ✅ = a NeoForge 1.21.1 build was directly found. ⚠️ = likely available but not directly confirmed in this pass — verify the exact build before installing.

| Type | Candidate mod(s) | Rationale | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal | Farmer's Delight | Broad, foundational, general-purpose content — the "does a bit of everything" type | ✅ |
| Fire | Powah! Rearchitected | Thermogenerators / heat-based power generation | ✅ (v6.1.5+ on NeoForge 1.21.1) |
| Water | Aquaculture 2 | Fishing, water loot, water-tied crafting | ✅ (2.7.x/2.8.x on 1.21.1) |
| Electric | Mekanism, Immersive Engineering | Wired power, energy networks, industrial electricity | ✅ Mekanism confirmed on 1.21.1; ⚠️ IE — verify current build |
| Grass | Productive Bees | Pollination/ecosystem simulation; pairs with the already-planned Grassier Grass + Cobblemon Wild Spawn | ✅ (1.21.1 builds on Modrinth/CurseForge) |
| Ice | Cold Sweat | Temperature-based survival mechanic | ⚠️ verify current 1.21.1 build |
| Fighting | L_Ender's Cataclysm | Boss-fight content — "prove your resonance through trial" | ✅ (2.5x+ on NeoForge 1.21.1) |
| Poison | Occultism | Ritual/sacrifice/otherworldly-familiar theming | ✅ (1.21.1-neoforge builds on Modrinth) |
| Ground | Terralith | Biome/terrain diversity — directly reinforces ground-type world affinity | ✅ (v2.6.2 NeoForge 1.21.1) |
| Flying | Alex's Mobs (Unofficial Port) | Adds flying fauna | ✅ confirmed CurseForge listing for 1.21.1 |
| Psychic | Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks | Eldritch/void spell school reads strongly psychic | ✅ (3.1x+ on 1.21.1) |
| Bug | Productive Bees | Dual-typed pick with Grass (bees are genuinely both) | ✅ |
| Rock | Create | Mechanical quarrying/processing; matches Wesley's own "Create → steel" instinct | ✅ widely available on NeoForge 1.21.1; already Tier 2 provisional in the M.M.I. |
| Ghost | Twilight Forest | Spectral enemies, dark dimension biomes | ✅ (4.6–4.8.x on MC 1.21.1) |
| Dragon | Ice and Fire: Dragons Port, or IceAndFire Community Edition | Literal dragons — two rival NeoForge continuations of the same original mod, pick one | ✅ both confirmed on NeoForge 1.21.1 |
| Dark | Occultism, Twilight Forest | Ritual/sacrifice theming + dark dimension biomes — both dual-typed from above | ✅ |
| Steel | Create, Immersive Engineering | Matches Wesley's own example exactly | ✅ Create confirmed; ⚠️ IE — verify current build |
| Fairy | Twilight Forest, Ars Nouveau | Fairy-tale fauna/biomes + whimsical glyph-based magic | ✅ both confirmed on NeoForge 1.21.1 |

**Explicitly ruled out despite being the original inspiration:** Astral Sorcery and the classic Blood Magic. Neither has a reliable official NeoForge 1.21.1 port — an unofficial/early community Blood Magic port exists on GitHub (`alfieparkin8/BloodMagic-1.21.1`) but isn't recommended as a foundation yet. Their *mechanics* (starlight flow; per-chunk corruption alignment) remain valid design inspiration for the Affinity Core itself — see the diffusion rework in `affinity-architecture.md` — even though the mods aren't being installed.

**Not yet decided:** whether any of these become real Tier 2 M.M.I. entries, or stay reference-only inspiration the way Astral Sorcery/Blood Magic ended up. That decision should go through the normal M.M.I. process, not get auto-adopted from this research pass.

## Archive Intake — 2026-09-19: Affinity as a Source-like energy network (unconfirmed)

Wesley + ChatGPT explored whether Affinity's generation/storage/transport should be modeled directly on **Ars Nouveau's Source system** (Source as a moved/stored energy medium; Sourcelinks generate it, Source Jars store it, Source Relays move it between devices), rather than Affinity being purely an abstract stat.

**The proposed architecture (not adopted, not built — pure idea):**

| Ars Nouveau concept | Proposed Affinity equivalent |
|---|---|
| Source | Affinity / Aethum-derived energy |
| Sourcelink | Affinity Generator/Link |
| Source Jar | Affinity Jar |
| Source Relay | Affinity Relay |
| Source generation | Affinity generation |
| Source-consuming machine | Affinity-consuming machine |

**Core idea:** Source = a general, untyped magical-energy medium; Affinity = Source that has been *attuned* to a specific one of the 18 principles (`Source → attunement → Fire Affinity`, etc.). This was explicitly proposed as a way to resolve Wesley's own worry that "liquid Source" and "liquid Affinity" might be contradictory concepts — the resolution offered is that they aren't the same liquid, they're the same medium at different attunement states. Also proposed: an **Affinity Seed** that generates its type's Affinity when planted/grown (a Sourcelink equivalent), feeding an **Affinity Jar** (a Source Jar equivalent) that machines/rituals draw from.

**Important finding surfaced while checking this idea:** a real, separate Minecraft mod is literally named **"Affinity"** — built around its own energy concepts called "Aethum" and "Aethum Flux," framed as fundamental life energy and its semi-physical counterpart. Confirmed present on Modrinth/CurseForge at an early version (`0.1.1`–`0.1.4`, tagged `[1.21+]`). This is **not** the source of the Source/Sourcelink idea above (that's genuinely Ars Nouveau's system) — it's a coincidental name collision with C.E.R.'s own "Affinity" system that's worth Wesley knowing about, independent of whether this Source-network idea goes anywhere. Being an early 0.1.x mod, it isn't being proposed as an install — just flagged so "Affinity" isn't assumed to be a name C.E.R. invented uncontested.

**Status: genuinely open, not decided.** This would be a substantial architecture choice (whether Affinity has a real, moveable, storable in-world form at all, vs. staying a pure behind-the-scenes stat consumed only through the `/cer` API / Core). Tracked as a real decision item in `claude/CER_Unanswered_Questions.md` and flagged (one line, not adopted) in `claude/affinity-architecture.md`'s Open Questions. Nothing about the Resource economy section of `affinity-architecture.md` (Resin, Affinity Metal) has been changed to reflect this — that section describes the currently-standing design, which does not (yet) include a Source-style network.

---

# C.E.R. — Governance & Workflow (F.R.M.)

Locked Free Reign Mode (F.R.M.) governance principles, working patterns, the Sweep Suite pointer, and the open governance proposals awaiting Wesley's sign-off.

## Locked governance principles

1. **Bridge-Eligible Mod Principle** — 4-step evaluation order for Fabric-only mods: (1) native port → (2) Connector/Forgified Fabric API → (3) alternative → (4) weigh the burden of forcing it in anyway.
2. **Mental Economy Delegation Principle** — small/cosmetic/QoL mods serve a genuinely necessary cognitive-rest function distinct from deep systemic mods; "lower-stakes" must never be read as "lower priority."
3. **Integration Depth Tiers** — Direct / Indirect / Observational / Social tiers for how mods connect to Affinity/Resonance, preventing every integration from becoming a flat Affinity trigger.
4. **Synergy Combos** (M.M.I. section) — small mods are evaluated as combinations, not just standalone candidates.

## Working patterns

- Mod verification is rigorous: confirmed against live sources for loader compatibility, Cobblemon version targeting, feature sets, and download counts before an M.M.I. entry is made.
- Mod submissions often come in loosely (misspellings, partial names, mixed source types) — batch-processed and disambiguated systematically.
- Design decisions are formalized as locked governance principles here once proven, not before.
- Redundancy clusters are resolved through structured sweeps (see Sweep Suite below), not ad hoc decisions.
- Philosophical coherence (e.g., scarcity design in Retirement/Championship Protocol) is treated as a hard constraint that can override convenience or feature richness.

## Sweep Suite (status: CONFIRMED, locked 2026-09-18)

The full C.E.R. sweep methodology is a fused taxonomy of **19 named sweeps** (Mod Inventory, Redundancy & Overlap, Implementation Layer, Compatibility & Version, Worldgen Integrity, Progression & Economy, Quest Design, Fit & Identity, Feature Coverage & Integration, Client & Input, Performance & Load, Stability, Architecture Integrity, Persistence & Multiplayer, Exploit & Abuse, Discovery & Design Philosophy, Build Validation, Playtest, Archive Sweep) plus four composite processes:

- **TriSweep** — light Mod Inventory + Redundancy & Overlap + Fit & Identity, for routine maintenance.
- **Final Pre-Release Sweep** — all 19 minus Archive Sweep, ship-gated.
- **Total Cleanse** — all 19 + both Archive Sweep modes, full project reset-and-verify (pack **and** documentation). This document set was produced by a Total Cleanse pass on the documentation side on 2026-09-18.
- **Targeted Regression Sweep** — only the sweeps a new feature actually touches.

Built by fusing ~73 ChatGPT-proposed micro-sweeps + 6 meta-processes at Wesley's direction. Full detail: `claude/CER_Sweep_Suite_FullTaxonomy.md`. Original verbatim source: `claude/CER_Sweep_Suite_Source.md`. Cheat-sheet: `claude/CER_Sweeps_Quick_Reference.md`. **These three docs are the confirmed source of record and are not rewritten by other passes** — only referenced.

**Archive Sweep** has two modes, both Wesley-coined terms:
- **Archive Intake** — the additive mode: fold new discussion into the archive before it's forgotten.
- **Archive Diet** — the subtractive mode: trim non-load-bearing "fluff" from an archive that's gotten "thick," without cutting anything decision-relevant. A trim, not a purge — when in doubt whether something is fluff, it stays.

Prior provisional sweep terms (Mod Audit, Modification Sweep, earlier "Optimization Sweep"/Compatibility & Version/Terminology-Consistency/Balance-Numbers/Archive-Memory proposals) are all superseded/absorbed into the fused taxonomy — see the FullTaxonomy doc's "fate of prior sweep terms" table for the exact mapping.

## The two new headline terms

- **Archive Diet** — going through already-compiled archive material and trimming "fluff": content that's related to a topic but not actually load-bearing for understanding or rebuilding it. A trim, not a purge — nothing decision-relevant gets cut, and unclear cases stay in by default. Run periodically once an archive file gets "thick." Companion to **Archive Intake** (moving new in-progress discussion into the archive in the first place) — together these make up the new **Archive Sweep**.
- **Total Cleanse** — the single most exhaustive pass that exists: every fused sweep below, plus both Archive Sweep modes, run in Master Workflow order. Broader than Final Pre-Release Sweep because it also audits the project's own documentation/memory, not just the pack. Reserve for major milestones or a full project reset-and-verify.

### 13. `CER_Sweep_Suite_FullTaxonomy.md`

# C.E.R. — Sweep Suite (Fused Taxonomy, Working Reference)

**Status:** CONFIRMED — this is the official, working sweep methodology going forward. Built by fusing the 73 micro-sweeps + 6 meta-processes ChatGPT proposed (preserved verbatim in `CER_Sweep_Suite_Source.md`) into a smaller set of named, overarching sweeps, per Wesley's explicit direction to integrate/optimize/fuse/rework using F.R.M. discretion. Every original micro-sweep still exists conceptually — it's now a named **check** inside one of the 19 fused sweeps below, not lost. This doc is the one to actually use day-to-day; the quick reference (`CER_Sweeps_Quick_Reference.md`) is the cheat-sheet version of this.

---

## The 19 fused sweeps

### 1. Mod Inventory Sweep
*Absorbs: MMI Sweep, Mod List Deduplication Sweep, Dependency/Library Sweep, Mod Purpose Sweep, MMI Confidence Sweep, Candidate→Confirmed Promotion Sweep.*
The master-inventory pass. Reconciles every mod source into one canonical MMI; checks for duplicate/renamed mods, loader variants, true dependency footprint, and confirms every entry can state its own purpose and carries an honest confidence tag (CONFIRMED / LIKELY / POTENTIAL / UNVERIFIED / REJECTED). This is what "Mod Audit" always meant — now formalized with real sub-checks instead of being a loose catch-all term.

### 2. Redundancy & Overlap Sweep
*Absorbs: Redundancy Sweep, Functionality Overlap Sweep, Feature Saturation Sweep, Replacement-vs-Integration Sweep, "Remove One Mod" Sweep.*
Asks whether something is being done more than once — as an outright duplicate, a partial functional overlap, or simple category saturation (too many biome/cave/structure mods even if none duplicate exactly) — and, for any hit, whether the fix is replace, merge, justify-both, or just delete one and see what breaks.

### 3. Implementation Layer Sweep
*Absorbs: Implementation Layer Sweep, KubeJS vs Mod vs Datapack Sweep, Configuration-First Sweep, Custom Mechanics Feasibility Sweep.*
For every desired feature: what's the lowest-complexity layer that can do it correctly (Vanilla → Datapack → KubeJS → mod config → mod integration → custom addon → custom mod)? Never reach for more power than the job needs. This is the same principle already locked as a proposed 5th F.R.M. governance principle — this sweep is its enforcement mechanism.

### 4. Compatibility & Version Sweep
*Absorbs: Compatibility Sweep, Cobblemon Compatibility Sweep, Version Drift Sweep, Update Regression Sweep, Config Conflict Sweep.*
Confirms every retained mod actually works in *our exact* environment — Minecraft/NeoForge/Cobblemon/KubeJS versions, required APIs, and Cobblemon-specific surfaces (battles, capture, spawning, evolution, breeding, riding, storage) — and re-checks this after any version bump or major update, not just at intake. (This is the sweep the Cobblemon 1.8.0→1.7.3 Snap-crash revert this session should have triggered proactively.)

### 5. Worldgen Integrity Sweep
*Absorbs: Worldgen Conflict Sweep, Worldgen Density/Chaos Sweep.*
Checks that terrain, biomes, caves, structures, dimensions, Aero Islands, and Pokémon structures coexist rather than overwrite or multiply into chaos, and that the resulting world *feels* intentionally authored rather than merely non-crashing.

### 6. Progression & Economy Sweep
*Absorbs: Progression Redundancy Sweep, Progression Gate Sweep, Progression Bypass Sweep, Recipe/Acquisition Sweep, Economy Sweep, Automation/Infinite Resource Sweep, Loot Table Sweep, Quest Reward Economy Sweep. Future check folded in: the previously-proposed Balance/Numbers Sweep, once numeric tuning becomes relevant.*
Maps every progression system and every way to acquire every important item/resource, and checks that gates are meaningful, unbypassed, rewards aren't accidentally trivializing the rest of the pack's economy, and nothing becomes silently infinite through automation.

### 7. Quest Design Sweep
*Absorbs: Quest Sweep.*
Reviews quest structure end to end (intro → early game → exploration → Cobblemon → technology → magic → Affinity → Fracture → endgame) for redundant/missing quests, unclear objectives, gates, and discovery pacing. Reward-economy concerns are handled by Progression & Economy Sweep (#6); this one is about structure and pacing.

### 8. Fit & Identity Sweep
*Absorbs: "Cool But Doesn't Belong" Sweep, "Can We Actually Use This?" Sweep, Thematic Cohesion Sweep, Modpack Identity Sweep, Lore/Mechanics Consistency Sweep, and the previously-proposed Terminology/Consistency Sweep.*
The philosophical gate: does this reinforce C.E.R.'s identity, does the lore/mechanics/terminology stay internally consistent, and — stripped of mod names — would this still read as C.E.R. rather than a generic kitchen-sink pack? Also where a mod with a great concept but a poor real-world implementation gets caught before it's adopted.

### 9. Feature Coverage & Integration Sweep
*Absorbs: Feature-to-Mod Coverage Sweep, Integration Opportunity Sweep, Integration Gap Sweep, Cobblemon Ecosystem Sweep, "What Are We Missing?" Sweep, and the Reverse Audit / Interaction Audit / Integration Value Audit meta-processes.*
Works backward from design intent instead of forward from the mod list: what does C.E.R. actually need, what already covers it, what's missing, what two existing systems should be talking to each other but aren't, and how much cross-system value does a given mod unlock (not just its standalone feature count)?

### 10. Client & Input Sweep
*Absorbs: Client QoL Saturation Sweep, Keybind/Input Sweep.*
Checks UI/tooltip/inventory/HUD/map/keybind mods for duplicate functionality, clutter, and keybind conflicts, so the controls and interface don't become their own unmanageable pile.

### 11. Performance & Load Sweep
*Absorbs: Performance Sweep, Tick/Polling Sweep, Server Tick Cost Sweep, Chunk Loading Sweep, Entity Population Sweep, Memory/RAM Sweep, Startup/Load-Time Sweep.*
Covers everything about speed and resource cost — client FPS, server TPS, tick-frequency of scripts (prefer event/interval/state-change over polling — critical for Affinity thresholds), chunk-loading footprint, entity counts, RAM, and startup time.

### 12. Stability Sweep
*Absorbs: Crash/Error Sweep, Log Spam Sweep.*
Categorizes every crash and log warning by root cause (mod bug, dependency, config, script, worldgen, entity, rendering, memory, version mismatch) and asks whether it points to a deeper architectural problem rather than just "remove the mod."

### 13. Architecture Integrity Sweep
*Absorbs: Datapack Priority/Load Order Sweep, Script Namespace/Architecture Sweep, Hardcoded Value Sweep, State Ownership Sweep, Single Source of Truth Sweep, State Synchronization Sweep, and the Ownership Audit / Complexity Budget Audit / Maintenance Debt meta-processes.*
The Affinity lesson, generalized: who owns each piece of state, is it stored in exactly one authoritative place, are shared constants centralized instead of hardcoded in ten scripts, is the KubeJS folder structure sane, and — at milestones — what has been built that future-us will hate maintaining?

### 14. Persistence & Multiplayer Sweep
*Absorbs: Save/Restart Persistence Sweep, Multiplayer/Server Scope Sweep, FTB Teams Interaction Sweep.*
For every custom system: does it survive logout/restart/reload/dimension-travel/death, and is its scope (player/team/region/world/server) actually what's intended — especially before tying Affinity into Teams-based quests.

### 15. Exploit & Abuse Sweep
*Absorbs: Exploit Sweep, AFK/Automation Abuse Sweep, Player Behavior Sweep.*
Deliberately tries to break every major system (repeat/automate/reset/multiply/multi-player-trigger), checks the 12-hours-AFK case, and separately asks what a *non-malicious* player would naturally be drawn to do — flagging any mechanic whose "optimal" play is degenerate.

### 16. Discovery & Design Philosophy Sweep
*Absorbs: Discovery/Prescription Sweep.*
Kept as its own named sweep (rather than folded into Fit & Identity) because Discovery Over Prescription is a locked core pillar, not just a style preference: checks quests, item text, and system introductions for over-explaining mechanics the player should be finding for themselves.

### 17. Build Validation Sweep
*Absorbs: Proof-of-Concept Sweep, Vertical Slice Sweep, End-to-End Integration Sweep.*
The staged way any new ambitious system gets built: smallest possible prototype first, then one complete end-to-end example, then confirmation that the full chain (Cobblemon → KubeJS → C.E.R. → Affinity → FTB → reward → next stage) actually works together — never all 18 Affinities implemented before knowing one works.

### 18. Playtest Sweep
*Absorbs: Player Experience Sweep, Fresh-World Sweep, Blind Playtest Sweep, Endgame/Long-Term Loop Sweep.*
Actually playing the pack rather than auditing it on paper — as a normal player, from a completely fresh world with no dev commands, ideally by someone blind to the architecture, and separately from an endgame/100+-hour perspective to check what's still meaningful that far out.

### 19. Archive Sweep *(new family — not in the source text; established this session to fill a real gap)*
Covers the project's own documentation/memory health, in two modes:
- **Archive Intake** *(was "Archive/Memory Sweep")* — the additive mode: moves in-progress design discussion (chat, sessions) into properly structured, indexed archive/project docs before it's forgotten.
- **Archive Diet** *(new term, established this session at Wesley's request)* — the subtractive mode: goes through already-compiled archive material and strips "fluff" — content that's related to a topic but not actually load-bearing for understanding or rebuilding it — without touching the substantive decisions, reasoning, or history those archives exist to preserve. This is a *trim*, not a *purge*: nothing decision-relevant gets cut, and the archival philosophy of "preserve uncertainty rather than invent it" still applies — if it's unclear whether something is fluff, it stays.

These two modes are companions, not competitors: Intake grows the archive to keep it complete; Diet keeps that growth from calcifying into bloat. Run Intake after any substantial design session; run Diet periodically once an archive file gets "thick" (Wesley's own word for the trigger condition).

---

## Composite / umbrella processes

### TriSweep *(retained, redefined)*
The lightweight, frequent-use version: a quick pass of **Mod Inventory Sweep + Redundancy & Overlap Sweep + Fit & Identity Sweep**. Originally "running all three sweeps together as one optimized process" — now each of the three is itself a proper fused sweep, so TriSweep is the routine maintenance check between bigger passes, not the exhaustive one.

### Final Pre-Release Sweep *(retained)*
The release-gate chain, run in order, then the build is frozen:
Mod Inventory → Compatibility & Version → Worldgen Integrity → Progression & Economy → Quest Design → Performance & Load → Stability → Architecture Integrity → Persistence & Multiplayer → Exploit & Abuse → Playtest → Fit & Identity.

### Total Cleanse *(new term, established this session at Wesley's request)*
The maximal pass — **every one of the 19 fused sweeps above, plus both Archive Sweep modes, run in Master Workflow order.** This is the thing Final Pre-Release Sweep doesn't quite reach: it audits the pack *and* the project's own documentation/memory together, so it isn't only a "ready to ship" gate — it's a full reset-and-verify for the whole system, pack and archive alike. Reserve it for major milestones or whenever the entire project (not just the build) needs a clean bill of health. Final Pre-Release Sweep is effectively Total Cleanse minus the two Archive Sweep modes, scoped specifically to shipping.

### Targeted Regression Sweep *(retained as a standing meta-process, not a one-time sweep)*
After any major addition, don't run Total Cleanse — run only the fused sweeps whose domain the new feature actually touches. Example: adding Affinity would trigger Architecture Integrity, Compatibility & Version (Cobblemon-side), Progression & Economy, Persistence & Multiplayer, Exploit & Abuse, Discovery & Design Philosophy, and Client & Input (its UI) — not a blind retest of everything.

---

| **Optimization Sweep** *(my provisional reconstruction, last session)* | Confirmed as the right instinct — formalized as **Redundancy & Overlap Sweep** (#2). |

| **Balance/Numbers Sweep** *(my proposal, last session, flagged future)* | Folded into **Progression & Economy Sweep** (#6) as a future-phase check, still flagged as not urgent until numeric tuning starts. |

## Master workflow (unchanged in spirit, sweep names updated)

```
DESIGN → what do we want?
↓
Feature Coverage & Integration Sweep (reverse-audit half) → what provides it?
↓
Mod Inventory Sweep
↓
Redundancy & Overlap Sweep
↓
Compatibility & Version Sweep
↓
Implementation Layer Sweep
↓
Build Validation Sweep (prototype → vertical slice → end-to-end)
↓
Progression & Economy Sweep
↓
Exploit & Abuse Sweep
↓
Performance & Load Sweep
↓
Persistence & Multiplayer Sweep
↓
Playtest Sweep
↓
Fit & Identity Sweep
↓
SHIP
```

Archive Sweep (both modes) runs alongside this loop on its own cadence, not as a gate in the ship path — it keeps the record of *why* the loop happened intact and lean, rather than blocking the loop itself.
